name: Business websites
promise: A branded site that represents your business around the clock.
blurb: The core build. Three packages, each a one-time price agreed before I start.
intro: Most people looking for a business like yours will decide whether to call you before they ever speak to you. They will do it on a phone, in under a minute, from a search result. A business website exists to win that minute.
That means the essentials come first: what you do, where you are, what it costs, and how to get hold of you. Everything else is arranged around those four.
Every build is custom-coded rather than assembled from a template, which is why it loads fast on mobile data and why changing something later does not mean fighting a page builder.
includes: Home, services, about and contact pages
Contact and quote forms that reach your inbox
Google Maps, hours and click to call
On-page SEO built in, not sold back to you
Hosting, SSL and backups on your care plan
Built for phones first

faq.q: What do you need from me to start?
faq.a: Your logo if you have one, photos of your own work, and a rough idea of what you want each page to say. If you have none of that, content preparation covers me gathering it with you. It is a listed fee between $100 and $175, not a surprise.

faq.q: Who owns the site when it is done?
faq.a: You do, and you own the domain outright because you bought it in your own name. The care plan covers hosting and updates, not custody of your own business.

faq.q: Why is a care plan required?
faq.a: A site nobody hosts, backs up or patches is not a working site. The plan starts at $45 a month, covers hosting, SSL, backups and monitoring, and includes edits. There is a 3-month minimum and then you can cancel with 30 days' notice.

name: Menu and services pages
promise: Everything you offer, on one page a customer can actually read.
blurb: Food, nails, detailing, lawn care. Any business with a list.
intro: A printed menu photographed and uploaded as a PDF is the most common mistake a small business makes online. It is unreadable at arm's length on a phone, invisible to Google, and out of date the day a price changes.

A real menu or services page is text. It scales to the screen, it can be searched, and changing a price takes a minute instead of a reprint. It works exactly the same whether you are listing tacos, nail treatments, detailing packages or lawn services.
Past about 20 items the job changes shape: it needs categories, filtering and a layout that survives scrolling. That is where the complex price applies, and it is the only thing that moves it.
includes: Every item as real text, not an image of text
Prices you can change without a redesign
Categories and sections once the list is long
Photos per item where you have them
Readable at arm's length on a phone

faq.q: What if I do not sell food?
faq.a: Then it is a services page and it works identically. A lawn care company listing five services and a restaurant listing sixty items are the same page with different amounts in it, which is exactly what simple and complex measure.

faq.q: Can I update the prices myself?
faq.a: Small price changes are covered by the edit allowance on your care plan, so you message me and it is done. If you want to make the changes yourself, self-editable content is a $225 power feature and it is built for exactly this.

name: Catering and quote pages
promise: Turn a big job enquiry into a lead you can actually follow up.
blurb: Lead capture for the jobs that need a conversation first.
intro: The jobs worth the most are the ones that need a conversation first: a wedding, a fleet, a full-property contract. Those enquiries arrive as a phone call you miss, or a message with none of the detail you need to quote.
A catering or quote page asks the right questions up front. You open your inbox to a date, a headcount and a budget instead of the word "hi".
The complex version is the one where the page also sells: your packages laid out, what each includes, and pricing tiers underneath them.
includes: A form that asks what you need in order to quote
Your packages laid out with what each includes
Enquiries delivered straight to your inbox
Works for catering, events, contracts or fleet work

faq.q: How is this different from the contact form?
faq.a: The contact form asks for a name and a message. This one asks the questions that decide whether you can take the job and what to charge for it: the date, the headcount, the specifics. It is the difference between an enquiry and a lead.

name: Booking integration
promise: Let clients book straight from your site, at any hour, without phone tag.
blurb: Calendly, Square, Booksy or Vagaro, wired into the site properly.
intro: Every booking made by phone costs you a call, and every call you miss costs you the booking. Someone deciding at nine at night will book the business that lets them and leave a voicemail for the one that does not.

I connect the booking system to your site so the availability people see is the availability you actually have, and so the booking buttons sit where someone has just decided to act rather than three scrolls below it.
If you take deposits or payment at the time of booking, that is a further $150 on top of either option. It is the part that stops no-shows, and it is worth costing separately rather than burying.

faq.q: Do I need an account already?
faq.a: No, but having one makes it a standard setup rather than a complex one, and that is one of the things the price measures. If you do not have one, I will set it up and configure your services with you.

Tell me how you take bookings today and I will tell you plainly. Most single-service businesses are well served by Calendly's free tier; salons and multi-staff operations usually need something like Square or Vagaro.

name: Care plans
promise: The site stays hosted, secure, backed up and current, without you touching it.
blurb: Required with every build. $45 or $95 a month.
intro: Hours change. Prices change. You get better photos. A site still showing last year's information does more damage than no site at all, because it teaches people your business cannot be trusted on detail.

A care plan is what keeps that from happening, and it is required with every build. That is not an upsell: a site nobody hosts, patches or backs up is not a working site, and I am not willing to hand over something that will quietly break six months later.
Host keeps the site online and current. Grow adds real monthly work on top: four updates, faster turnaround, and your Google Business Profile managed rather than just created.
includes: Hosting, SSL and daily backups
Uptime monitoring
Edits handled by me, with no CMS to learn
Google Business Profile management on Grow
A monthly performance report on Grow
3-month minimum, then 30 days' notice

faq.a: One request, however many small changes are in it. Sending four photos to swap is one update, not four. Host covers up to 15 minutes of edits a month; Grow covers four updates a month with a 3-business-day turnaround.

faq.q: How do I request a change?
faq.a: You message me. You get my number, not a ticket queue.

faq.q: What if I need more than my plan covers?
faq.a: Anything beyond the allowance is priced by size and published: $30 minor, $60 moderate, $100 substantial. You will get told which bracket a job lands in before I do it.
After the 3-month minimum, with 30 days' notice. The site is yours either way. I stop hosting it, nothing is deleted, and I will help you move it to your own hosting.

name: Google Business Profile
promise: The listing that shows up in the map pack, set up in your own account.
blurb: $200 standalone. Setup assistance in Standard and Complete, managed on Grow.
intro: For a local business, the Google Business Profile is often doing more work than the website is. It is the box with your hours, your photos, your reviews and a call button, and it appears above the search results rather than in them.

I set it up inside your own Google account, so it belongs to you and nobody has to ask my permission to change it later. Categories, service areas, hours, description, photos and the first review request all get handled.
Google controls verification timelines and anyone who promises you a date on that is guessing. What I can control is that everything is correct and complete the moment it goes live.
includes: Created or claimed in your own Google account
Categories and service areas chosen deliberately
Hours, description and contact details completed
Photos uploaded and named properly
Verification submitted and followed through
Posts and review responses handled on the Grow plan

pricing.note: Setup assistance is included in Standard and Complete. Ongoing management, posts and review responses are part of the Grow care plan at $95 a month.

faq.a: Yours. I work inside your Google account rather than creating one I control. If we part ways, the listing does not move.
Google decides that, and it ranges from a day to a few weeks depending on how they choose to verify you. I submit it and follow it through, but nobody can promise you a date.
It is the local half of it, and for a business with a service area it is usually the half that brings the phone calls. On-page SEO for the site itself is built into every package at no extra cost.

name: Business cards
promise: Cards that match the site exactly, so your brand looks the same on screen and in hand.
blurb: $85 basic, $165 premium. Same brand as the site.
intro: A card designed separately from the website always looks like it. Different blue, different typeface, a logo at a slightly different weight. Small differences that add up to a business that looks improvised.
Designing the card against the same brand as the site means the person who found you online and the person handed your card meet the same business.
Basic is design only: you get print-ready files and take them wherever you like. Premium is front and back on thick stock with a QR code, printed and delivered to you.
